title: August and the Alibi
premise: True-crime podcaster August Whitlock has built a quiet reputation solving deaths the police mislabeled as accidents, so when twin letters arrive—one confessing to a forty-year-old drowning, one promising 'more soon'—they recognize the handwriting of a case file only the killer could know. As August reopens the Hollow Creek drownings, they discover the confessor is someone inside their own circle, and each new letter arrives timed to a fresh death. The trap August sets in the flooded quarry where it all began forces a final confession, but exposing the killer means destroying the one person who ever made them feel they belonged—and August must choose truth over loyalty, broadcasting the ending live.
about_author: Beatrix Blackwood is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent two decades transcribing small-town tragedies before turning them into fiction. She writes from a farmhouse in upstate New York, where the well water still tastes faintly of iron.

chapters.title: Twin Envelopes
chapters.summary: August's POV. Opening two letters postmarked the same day: a full confession to the 1984 drowning of Lena Marsh, and a second note reading 'more soon.' The emotional beat is vertigo—August's career has been built on other people's cold cases, and now one has chosen them personally.

chapters.title: The File That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: August cross-references the confession against sealed records and finds details never made public—the color of Lena's shoelaces, the position of her body. POV shifts to Detective Rosa Ibarra, who once leaked August a file and now warns them off. Beat: unease deepening into obsession.

chapters.title: Hollow Creek Revisited
chapters.summary: August travels to the dying mill town where Lena drowned, interviewing the victim's aged sister. They learn there were three drownings in four years, all ruled accidental. Beat: the thrill of the hunt curdling as August realizes the town has been protecting someone for decades.

chapters.title: The Circle
chapters.summary: Back home, August's found-family podcast crew—producer Dev, sound engineer Marisol, and mentor figure Elias Crane—are introduced in full. A third letter arrives at the studio itself. Beat: warmth and belonging established precisely so its loss will hurt later.

chapters.title: More Soon
chapters.summary: A fourth death surfaces: a retired coroner from Hollow Creek, drowned in his bathtub. The letter that follows describes it before police release details. August's POV frays between grief and grim validation—they were right about everything, and being right has killed someone. Beat: guilt.

chapters.title: Elias Knows Things
chapters.summary: August notices their mentor deflecting questions about Hollow Creek with practiced ease. A flashback chapter in Elias's POV, 1984: a young man watching Lena Marsh walk to the creek, told obliquely enough to implicate anyone. Beat: dread planted in the reader without confirmation.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: August breaks into the county records office with Dev's help and photographs the original case files—finding pages razored out. Someone has been editing history for forty years. Beat: the mystery shifts from 'who killed' to 'who is still covering.'

chapters.title: Marisol's Silence
chapters.summary: Marisol, whose family emigrated from Hollow Creek, goes strangely quiet when the town comes up. August confronts her gently; she admits her grandmother was Lena's best friend but refuses to say more. Beat: loyalty beginning to strain against truth within the crew.

chapters.title: A Letter Addressed to You
chapters.summary: The killer's letters turn personal, referencing August's childhood in foster care—details no stranger could know. August realizes the confessor isn't just watching the investigation; they've known August far longer than August knew. Beat: violation; the hunter becomes the hunted.

chapters.title: Three Graves, One Stone
chapters.summary: August locates the unmarked graves of the other two victims and finds fresh flowers on all three. Stakeout footage catches a figure too blurred to identify—but wearing a coat August recognizes. Beat: suspicion turns inward on the found family, and August hates themselves for it.

chapters.title: What Dev Didn't Upload
chapters.summary: Auditing studio archives, August finds deleted audio from an old episode—Elias and Dev discussing Hollow Creek years ago, voices tense. Confrontation splits the crew. Beat: paranoia fully blooms; every act of kindness now reads as possible manipulation.

chapters.title: The Confession Tape
chapters.summary: A package arrives: a cassette of a man confessing to all three drownings in 1988—a confession that was buried. The voice is young Elias. August must decide whether the tape proves guilt or whether someone is framing their mentor. Beat: the floor drops out of everything August believes.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Firelight
chapters.summary: August plays the tape for Elias at his cabin. He neither confirms nor denies, instead telling a story about a town that decided who belonged and who didn't—and what he did to survive being on the wrong side of that line. Beat: sympathy weaponized; the reader wavers.

chapters.title: Rosa's Cold Case Wall
chapters.summary: Detective Ibarra, off the record, shows August her private wall: she's been tracking the letters for months and suspects the current killings are cover for something else entirely—the drownings were never the point. Beat: the case inverts; August has been chasing the wrong crime.

chapters.title: The Fifth Letter
chapters.summary: A letter names the next victim: Marisol. Deadline: the anniversary of Lena's death, six days away. August must choose between protecting her by pulling her from the story or using her as bait. Beat: loyalty versus truth made literal and unbearable.

chapters.title: Bait
chapters.summary: Against Ibarra's objections, the crew stages Marisol's public return to Hollow Creek, feeding the killer a false timeline through the podcast feed. August narrates lies on air for the first time in their career. Beat: self-betrayal; the truth-teller becomes a liar to catch a liar.

chapters.title: Anniversary Eve
chapters.summary: Stakeout in the rain-soaked town. Everything goes wrong: the killer anticipates the trap, Dev is injured, and August spots the coat from the graveyard—on Elias. He vanishes into the dark. Beat: betrayal confirmed, or so it seems; despair at its lowest ebb.

chapters.title: The Quarry
chapters.summary: August follows Elias to the flooded quarry where Lena died. There he reveals the truth: he was a witness, not a killer—the drownings were the work of the town patriarchs, and the letters are from the last surviving one, tying loose ends before dying. Beat: revelation reframing everything.

chapters.title: Drowning Season
chapters.summary: The true killer—respected town elder Harold Voss—arrives to finish the job, having used August's podcast to flush out witnesses. Confrontation at the water's edge; Elias takes a blow meant for August. Beat: climax; violence, confession, and the cost of forty years of silence converging.

chapters.title: Live Broadcast
chapters.summary: With Voss arrested and Elias hospitalized, August faces the choice: bury Elias's complicity in the cover-up or tell the whole truth. They go live and broadcast everything—including the parts that hurt. Beat: the theme resolved; truth chosen over loyalty, at real price.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Aftermath: the crew fractured but intact, Marisol reconciling with her grandmother's memory, Dev recovering. Elias, facing charges, tells August he doesn't regret being caught by someone worth confessing to. Beat: bittersweet reckoning with identity—who August is when the case ends.

chapters.title: The Empty Mailbox
chapters.summary: Final chapter, August's POV, weeks later. No more letters. August visits Lena's restored grave, leaves flowers, and records a short epilogue: some cases aren't solved, they're survived. Then a single new envelope appears—not a threat, but a thank-you note from a stranger with a cold case of her own. Beat: quiet hope; the cycle continues, chosen this time.
